profile.summary: GenePT builds gene and cell embeddings from text instead of training on expression data. Each gene's NCBI summary is embedded with an OpenAI text embedding model; a cell embedding is then either the expression-weighted average of its gene embeddings (GenePT-w) or the text embedding of the cell's gene names ordered by expression (GenePT-s). The embeddings feed gene-level and cell-level tasks such as gene property and cell type classification.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: What is GenePT?; paper Methods 3.1

summary_quotes.text: GenePT offers a complementary approach by using NCBI text descriptions of individual genes combined with GPT-3.5 to generate gene embeddings.
(i) by averaging the gene embeddings, weighted by each gene’s expression level; or (ii) by creating a sentence embedding for each cell, using gene names ordered by expression level.
we developed two distinct approaches: GenePT-w (w for weighted) and GenePT-s (s for sentence)

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: About 33,000 genes were taken from the scGPT and Geneformer vocabularies and genes in the downstream datasets. Each gene's NCBI summary was embedded with text-embedding-ada-002, giving a 1,536-dimensional gene vector. For cells, counts are normalised to 10,000 per cell and log(1 + x) transformed. GenePT-w takes the expression-weighted average of the gene vectors and scales it to unit length. GenePT-s writes the expressed gene names in descending order of expression as a sentence and embeds that sentence. No model is trained on expression data.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The released artefact is a set of precomputed gene embeddings on Zenodo (record 10833191, one zip file). In March 2024 the authors added embeddings that include UniProt protein summaries and embeddings from the newer text-embedding-3-large model, alongside the original text-embedding-ada-002 ones. A result should state which summary file and which embedding model were used, since GenePT-w results depend on that choice.

strengths.text: No pre-training on expression data and no dataset curation; a cell embedding is a weighted average of precomputed gene vectors.

quotes.text: Without the need for dataset curation and additional pre-training, GenePT is efficient and user-friendly.

strengths.text: Precomputed gene embeddings and the gene summaries are public under CC BY 4.0.
The authors report performance comparable to, and often better than, single-cell foundation models on gene property and cell type classification (authors' claim).

quotes.text: GenePT achieves comparable, and often superior, performance to existing single-cell foundation models

limitations.text: Relies only on existing gene summaries, so poorly documented gene functions are missed, and the embeddings are not specific to a tissue or cell type (authors' own limitations).

quotes.text: the current GenePT framework only makes use of available gene summaries and descriptions. This may overlook the intricacies of lesser-known functionalities not documented in databases like NCBI.
GenePT embeddings might not be optimal for specific tissues and cell types

limitations.text: Making new gene embeddings, and every GenePT-s cell embedding, needs a registered OpenAI API account; the README links to OpenAI's pricing details.

no_run_guide_reason: GenePT has no installable package or command-line entry point. The repository provides Jupyter notebooks for the paper's analyses and the embeddings are a Zenodo download; the README gives no install or run commands.

notes: The record's reported name is GenePT-w, one of the two cell embedding variants; this page covers GenePT as a whole. scELMo (09-scelmo) is a related text-embedding method with its own repository and paper; the two records are not duplicates. The paper read is preprint v2 in PMC; the published version, if any, was not checked.
